clue.text: Noticed poles impeding top player

indicators.note: the poles get in the way of the player, standing in the middle of the word

parts.note: a seed is a top-ranked player in a tennis draw
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Someone spotted the magnetic poles obstructing a champion.
explanation.definitionFit: Sensed and noticed both mean perceived or became aware of something.

clue.text: Show wrong sign in European river

indicators.note: the cross sits within the letters for European and river

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
a cross, X, marks a wrong answer

explanation.surface: A misleading signpost stands in a continental river.
explanation.definitionFit: An expo is an exposition, a large public exhibition or trade show.

clue.text: Theory of self very much limits one's morals at first

parts.note: so as in 'so kind' means very much
lips are rims or edges, the limits of a vessel
one's is I'S, one is

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word morals is used

explanation.surface: A self-centred philosophy is said to cap one's ethics from the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: Solipsism holds that only one's own mind is sure to exist, a philosophy centred wholly on the self.

clue.text: Detective gets rough synopsis

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector

indicators.note: rough here means roughed up, so the letters of gets are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A police inspector receives a crude summary of the case.
explanation.definitionFit: A digest is a condensed summary of a longer text, as is a synopsis.

clue.text: Train sailor to grasp gallons and miles in Arabic maths

indicators.note: the rearranged sailor holds the gallons letter inside it
to train is to drill or school, so the letters of sailor are put into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to coach a seaman to handle imperial measures for his arithmetic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' reshuffles SAILOR into ALORIS, which then grasps G; M follows on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Algorism is the decimal system of reckoning with Arabic numerals, named after the mathematician al-Khwarizmi.

clue.text: Johnson's self-assessment: he's glad to work with 14

indicators.note: the letters are put to work, worked into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: the solution to 14 across, items in hearing

explanation.surface: Johnson is pleased to toil alongside another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Johnson's 1755 Dictionary defined a lexicographer as 'a writer of dictionaries; a harmless drudge', the theme of the puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Johnson, a lexicographer himself, gave this wry description of his own trade in his dictionary entry.

clue.text: Word list fool set up in delight

indicators.note: the upturned fool goes into the word for delight

parts.note: to glory in is to delight in

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word is written upwards

parts.note: an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A vocabulary list that some idiot has rigged to bring joy.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossary is an alphabetical list of terms with their meanings, a word list.

clue.text: Send on tablet stolen from joint

indicators.note: the pill is taken away from the word for a joint

parts.note: a reefer is a cannabis joint
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet

explanation.surface: A drug-themed picture: pills pinched from a spliff, and passed along.
explanation.definitionFit: To refer a case or patient is to send it on or pass it to someone else.

clue.text: Lock minutes in small cupboard as reading aid

indicators.note: the lock and minutes sit inside the small cupboard

parts.note: an ark is an old word for a chest or cupboard
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Someone shuts away the minutes of a meeting in a little cabinet for a reader.
explanation.definitionFit: A stress mark shows which syllable carries emphasis, helping a reader pronounce a word, as dictionaries do.

clue.text: It justifies a game I introduced to Georgia

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback

indicators.note: the letter I is put inside the abbreviation for the state

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: A sporting excuse: a horseback game brought to the state of Georgia.
explanation.definitionFit: An apologia is a formal written defence of one's conduct or opinions, a work that justifies.

clue.text: Old cross hides another one that's worn

indicators.note: the old crossing conceals a second cross inside itself

parts.note: to ford a river is to cross it
another cross, the letter X

explanation.surface: An angry old person hiding something else that's been worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' is first taken as FORD, then 'another' cross is the letter X. The answer is also the Oxford English Dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oxford is a style of lace-up leather shoe, something worn on the feet.

clue.text: Support film about extremely serious lady of letters

parts.note: a post is a supporting upright
a mist is a thin film, as on glass
re means about or concerning

indicators.note: the extreme letters, first and last, of the word serious

explanation.surface: A literary woman is the subject of a grave film being propped up.
explanation.definitionFit: She is a woman in charge of a post office, so handles letters, rather than being a writer.

clue.text: Deft old secretary HM enlisted shows patience with capital, maybe

parts.note: light as in a light touch means deft or nimble

indicators.note: the monarch is signed up inside the secretary's letters

parts.note: a PA is a personal assistant, a secretary
Her Majesty, the Queen, is ER, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A nimble former secretary recruited the Queen and displays forbearance with money.
explanation.walkthrough: With a capital P, Patience is a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera; 'maybe' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Patience is one of Gilbert and Sullivan's comic operettas, an example of the light opera genre.

clue.text: Anyone can edit this when it's keyed in at the start

indicators.note: only the opening letter of each of the four words is used

explanation.surface: A description of an open document that anyone may type into.
explanation.definitionFit: A wiki is a website, like Wikipedia, whose pages any user may revise collaboratively.

clue.text: A murder suspect finally admits items in hearing

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dodgy, so the letters are scrambled
the closing letter of the word admits

explanation.surface: A murder suspect eventually confesses to things raised at a court hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Eardrums are membranes in the ears that vibrate with sound, parts used in the act of hearing.

clue.text: Arcane ceremony involves topless runner-up

indicators.note: the ceremony wraps itself round the other piece

parts.note: a rite is a ceremony

indicators.note: the top letter, the first in a down clue, is removed

parts.note: the runner-up comes second

explanation.surface: A mysterious ritual features a second-placed athlete without a shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' leaves ECOND; the 'runner-up' is the one who finishes second, not an athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: Recondite means obscure, little known, understood only by a few, just as arcane does.

clue.text: Dramatist's The Old Weavers

definitions.meaning: belonging to John Webster, the Jacobean playwright of The Duchess of Malfi
webster is an obsolete word for a weaver, so these are weavers of old

explanation.surface: A playwright's work titled The Old Weavers.
explanation.walkthrough: Webster's is also the American dictionary, part of the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: John Webster wrote revenge tragedies, and in old English a webster was someone who wove cloth.

clue.text: Cleaners collect award for bar's accommodation

indicators.note: the cleaners gather up the award inside their word

parts.note: chars, charwomen, are cleaners
the MBE is a British honour, Member of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: Office cleaners pick up an honour for a pub's lodging rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub; it is the legal profession, the Bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Barristers practise from sets of offices called chambers, the premises of members of the Bar.

clue.text: Owner-occupier's about to secure centre

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the held letters run backwards
the letters are held securely inside the words owner and occupier

explanation.surface: Someone who owns their home is about to make the middle safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to secure' holds EROC inside OwnER-OCcupier; 'about' turns those letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: The core is the central part or heart of something, its centre.

clue.text: Right note upset acoustic device

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so read upwards

parts.note: a breve is a long musical note

explanation.surface: A right note sounding wrong has disturbed a piece of sound equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverb, short for reverberation, is an echo effect added by a sound unit to music.

clue.text: Audiences encourage junior theatre employee

parts.note: a house is a theatre audience, as in a full house
to urge on is to encourage

explanation.surface: Crowds cheer on a junior member of a playhouse staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theatre' suggests the stage, but it is an operating theatre in a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A house surgeon is a junior hospital doctor in surgery, working in operating theatres.

clue.text: American shorthand fast enough? Not entirely

indicators.note: the letters come from within the words fast enough, using only part of them

explanation.surface: A query whether a stenographer's speed is quite quick enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Steno is the American short word for stenography, writing in shorthand.

clue.text: Check out ancient coin in church

indicators.note: the coin sits within the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
the as was a bronze coin of ancient Rome

explanation.surface: Someone examines an old coin found in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: To case a place, as burglars do, is to inspect or check it out before acting.

clue.text: Latin law primarily explains Middle East language unit

parts.note: lex is the Latin word for law

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word explains

explanation.surface: Roman law chiefly explains the basics of an Arabic language unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A lexeme is a basic unit of vocabulary, such as run covering runs, ran and running.

clue.text: English teacher blocks new idea for hymn

indicators.note: the English teacher plugs a gap in the middle of the rearranged letters
new means made anew, so the letters of idea are put in a different order

parts.note: sir is how British pupils address a male teacher

explanation.surface: An English master stands in the way of a novel suggestion for a hymn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' gives the order DIAE; 'blocks' sets the teacher's letters inside it, after its first two.
explanation.definitionFit: Dies Irae, 'day of wrath', is a medieval Latin hymn sung in the Requiem Mass.

clue.text: Left son in to inspire French publisher

indicators.note: the son is placed within the word for inspire

parts.note: to arouse feelings is to inspire them

explanation.surface: A boy abandoned in an effort to motivate a Paris publishing house.
explanation.definitionFit: Larousse is the Parisian publisher famous for its French dictionaries and encyclopedias.

clue.text: Little brown jug for Guinness, say

parts.note: BR is a short form of brown
a ewer is a large water jug

explanation.surface: A small brown pitcher for a pint of Irish stout.
explanation.walkthrough: Brewer's Dictionary of Phrase and Fable fits the reference-book theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Guinness is a company that makes stout, so it is an example of a beer maker; 'say' marks the example.
